reason: The text explicitly portrays Hebrew leaders (the chorim/nobles and seganim/officials) as antagonistic toward the Hebrew people. The passage details complaints from common Jews that the leaders are: (1) exacting usury and forcing mortgages on fields, vineyards, and houses; (2) enslaving fellow Hebrews' children; and (3) exploiting the populace economically. Nehemiah directly confronts these leaders, saying 'You are exacting usury, each one from his brother' (v. 7), and compares their behavior unfavorably to previous governors who similarly 'laid heavy burdens on the people.' The leaders' antagonistic conduct toward their own people is the central focus of this passage.
